notes.title: v1.1.0 - Spout video routing
notes.content:
This update adds support for sending and receiving real-time video between Vinyl Reality and other applications (ex: OBS, Resolume, TouchDesigner, Processing) using Spout. 

Spout uses the GPU to send real-time video between Windows applications with near-zero latency or overhead.

Video can be sent to Spout from the spectator cameras in all environments in Vinyl Reality, including custom ones created with the SDK.

Vinyl Reality can also receive video from Spout and display it on the screens in the Streaming Studio and Indoor Rave environments.

Possible use cases for Spout in Vinyl Reality:

 Displaying custom visuals in the environments by receiving video from a VJ application
 Customizing your video streams by sending video to another application and adding effects
 Sending video directly to OBS for streaming

For more details on how to configure Spout in Vinyl Reality, be sure to check out the relevant documentation.

notes.title: v1.0 Released - Vinyl Reality leaves Early Access!
notes.content:
Today marks a very important milestone in Vinyl Reality’s development as it transitions from Early Access to a full release. 

Developing Vinyl Reality as a solo developer has been a very rewarding (and at times also a very challenging) experience, and I’m very proud of the final result. I feel that the application is now stable and delivers the experience that I initially set out to create.

I still have a lot of ideas on how to further improve the application, so of course this does not mean that there will be no new updates or content released in the future!

New promo videos

To help promote the full release of Vinyl Reality I’ve created two new videos. The first video is a brand new trailer which highlights some of the features that have been added during Early Access:

[previewyoutube=OFA0yF4KANc;full][/previewyoutube]
The second video is a bit more technical and gives a quick overview of all the DJ equipment currently available in the application:

[previewyoutube=2sRg-UJ3DgM;full][/previewyoutube]
Thank you!

I would like to thank everyone who has supported the development of Vinyl Reality during its Early Access phase. Getting this far wouldn’t have been possible without your continued support and amazing feedback! 

I hope you enjoy using the app as much as I’ve enjoyed creating it  💙

I’m currently working towards releasing the “full” version of Vinyl Reality and leaving Early Access, but I though it would be a good idea to release a small update in the meantime, with a couple of improvements and a new environment add-on.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/720d8ea812e08d06d3b0c9a8d9fc14e6b5d2e4ce.jpg

This environment is not included with the application by default, but can be downloaded from mod.io.

Be sure to also check out some of the other amazing environments which have been created by the community on Vinyl Reality's mod.io page!

 Beat Detection: Improved accuracy and responsiveness for all audio reactive components

Mod.io

To make it easier to share, discover and download user generated content for Vinyl Reality, I’ve setup a page for the application on mod.io, a cross platform mod API.

Content creators will be encouraged to upload their content to this page going forward, so that all of the custom environments and slipmats for Vinyl Reality are easily accessible in one place. An account is not needed to download content, but is required to upload it.

All of the custom content for Vinyl Reality can now be found at: https://vinylreality.mod.io/

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/b62bc930eecce0ef877c8a722b7c59cf228e4851.jpg

Installing custom content

For the time being, installing user generated content, still requires the files to be downloaded manually from the mod.io page, and then extracted and copied into the correct directory.

Install instructions for custom content can be found on the documentation wiki.

I hope to be able to integrate the mod.io API into Vinyl Reality at some point though, so that in the future content can be browsed and managed directly from inside the application.

Attic Environment

Some users might fondly remember the Attic environment which was included in early versions of Vinyl Reality, but was replaced by the Black Box and Streaming Studio in a recent update.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/4efbbbf9cb8263570b6f1e5dff872e373a51aee5.jpg

After making a few tweaks, this environment is now available again as a separate add-on and can also be downloaded from the mod.io page: https://vinylreality.mod.io/attic

notes.title: Audio filter effect and performance improvements
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/b3f67ba864e98a2f64d78b0f2c314221def582af.jpg

Low and High-Pass Filter

This release adds a new knob to each mixer channel, which combines a low and high-pass filter.

Turning the knob clockwise from the 12 o’clock position activates the high-pass filter (HPF), increasing the cutoff frequency from 20 to 22000hz when completely turned.

Turning the knob counter-clockwise, actives the low-pass filter (LPF), decreasing the cutoff frequency from 22000hz down to 20hz.

While the filter is active, the LED ring on the bottom of the knob is illuminated in blue.

The filter’s resonance and attenuation slope can also be configured in the mixer’s settings panel.

Known issues

Cross-platform Oculus avatars are currently not loading correctly. This issue is also affecting other applications and games, and is most likely caused by a problem with downloading the required assets from Oculus servers. 
I’ve contacted Oculus about the issue and hope it will be resolved on their end soon.

Full Release Notes
 Mixer: Added low and high-pass filter knob to each channel
 Mixer: Improved 3 band EQ knob sensitivity
 Mixer: Added filter resonance and slope to user settings
 Tech: Optimized performance

notes.title: Environments overhaul and streaming improvements
notes.content:
After two beta tests, the final version of update 1.3.0 is finally here! Here’s a quick overview of what’s new.

New EnvironmentsStreaming Studio A customizable environment with audio reactive video playback and lights
 Best suited for video recordings or live streams
 Optimized to run smoothly on machines meeting the minimum specs

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/7ae3335ba7bf59e973d1636eb5ad6a73ae744f6d.jpg

The Streaming Studio environment is specifically designed for streaming, by making it more visually interesting for people watching a video stream or recording made with Vinyl Reality, from outside of VR on a 2D screen. 

Users can customize the streaming studio environment by playing their own videos on the screens surrounding the DJ booth. More customization features might be added in upcoming updates.

Black Box A minimal, low-lit environment
 Best suited for long recording or practice sessions
 Optimized for performance

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/c41933004552c14948f14045ac59572ef31071e3.jpg

The Black Box environment was designed primarily with performance in mind, and should provide a very smooth DJing experience even on systems that only meet the minimum requirements. 

These two new environments replace the existing Attic and Recording Studio environments, but the plan is to make these available again as separate downloads in the near future, so they can be loaded as a custom environment.

Streaming Cameras
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/0beeb08ec093658970777f148c3d0e03b67a1d30.jpg

To give users more control over how streams are recorded, each environment now contains two spectator cameras that can be freely positioned anywhere inside the DJ booth. 
Both cameras can be activated using the existing streaming console. The camera to the left of the DJ gear is assigned to button number 3 on the streaming console and the one to right to button number 4.

For more information on how to use all of these new features, be sure to check out the online documentation for this update: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=early_access_v1.3.0f1

Full Release Notes: Environments: Added new Streaming Studio environment
 Environments: Added new Black Box environment
 Environments: Removed Attic and Recording Studio environments
 Streaming: Added two user controllable spectator cameras to all environments
 Streaming: Cross-platform Oculus avatar’s hand poses now update correctly for all platforms (except WMR)
 Streaming: Controller models are now hidden from spectator and mixed reality (LIV) cameras
 Streaming: The camera output screen now hides automatically when no spectator camera is active
 Bug: Fixed track cover artwork not loading when quality setting was set to low or medium
 Bug: Fixed Several minor bug fixes and improvements 
 Audio Analysis: Improved energy detection algorithm
 Oculus: Added correct models for Rift S controllers

notes.title: More streaming improvements and a new environment – Beta round 2
notes.content:
I wanted to give users more control over how streams are recorded, so I decided to add a new type of spectator camera that can be positioned anywhere in the environment and is activated using the existing streaming console. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/0beeb08ec093658970777f148c3d0e03b67a1d30.jpg

Each environment now contains two of these new user controllable cameras, one to the left of the DJ gear and one to the right. The left one is assigned to button number 3 on the streaming console and the right one to button number 4.

To position one of these cameras, simply grab it with a controller and move it to anywhere in the environment. The zoom level of the camera can also be adjusted, by moving the controller’s joystick or touchpad up and down (while selecting it with a controller).

New Environment
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/a1efafb4748d738c27cf10db45a47183b1a518dd.jpg

I’ve also replaced the recording studio environment with a new simple and low-lit environment called Black Box. This environment was designed primarily with performance in mind, and should provide a very smooth DJing experience even on systems that only meet the minimum requirements. 

The older environments that have been replaced by the Black Box and Streaming Studio will still be made available as a separate download once the final version of this update is released.

Full Release notes
 Environments: Added new Black Box environment, optimized for performance
 Streaming: Added two user controllable spectator cameras to all environments
 Streaming: The camera output screen now hides automatically when no spectator camera is active

notes.title: Streaming Studio Environment – Now in Beta!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/2f3e8369bcfb9591decba8323b1b121c3140b219.jpg

This beta release of Vinyl Reality adds an early version of the new Streaming Studio environment, which is specifically designed for streaming, by making it more visually interesting for people watching a video stream or recording made with Vinyl Reality, from outside of VR on a 2D screen.

Users can customize the environment by playing their own videos on the screens surrounding the DJ booth. More customization features will be added to the environment in upcoming updates.

To find out more about how to load your own videos, check out the online documentation on this topic.

I’d love to hear all of your feedback on this new environment, so be sure to share your thoughts in the beta testing forums, or on the Vinyl Reality Discord server!

Planned environments for the full release
In preparation for the full release of Vinyl Reality, I decided to rethink the environments included with the application, seeing what works and, more importantly, what I think could be improved.

For the final version of the app I'm planning to include 3 different types of environments, each serving a unique purpose:

 Minimal: Very simple and brightly lit environment, optimized for the best performance. Best suited for practicing and audio recording.
 Streaming: Designed to be as visually interesting as possible for spectators (on a 2D screen), with audio reactive lights, animations and visual effects. Designed to run smoothly on machines meeting the minimum specs. Will allow for some customization.
 Experience: Designed to be as realistic, immersive, visually interesting and awe-inspiring as possible from the perspective of the VR user. Will require a system with recommended specs to run smoothly.


The third type (experience) will probably only be added after the application leaves Early Access, because it will take a considerable amount of time and resources to create.

I plan to remove or redesign all of the current environments (Recording Studio, Attic and Club), but still make the current versions available as a separate download, so they can be loaded as a custom environment.

Full release notes
 Environments: Added an early version of Streaming Studio environment with customizable audio reactive video screens
 Streaming: Cross-platform Oculus avatar’s hand poses now update correctly for all platforms (except WMR)
 Streaming: Controller models are now hidden from spectator and mixed reality (LIV) cameras
 Bug: Fixed track cover artwork not loading when quality setting was set to low or medium

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.4
notes.content:
Early Access version 1.2.4 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds the final improvements to the record case before the upcoming full release of the application.

Vinyl Record Labels
My favorite new feature in this update is the ability to load and display the cover art embedded in audio files on the vinyl record’s label. I think it adds a really nice visual touch to the records and makes each one feel more unique and recognizable. 

If no front cover art image is embedded in a file, the old default record label will be used. As always, this feature is optional and can be configured in the new record case user settings panel.

Additional Metadata
I’ve redesigned the bottom part of the record case’s UI and replaced the mostly useless navigation menu options UI with a display for the selected track's key, length and genre metadata.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/1933d3a7537de0c5224907885d601d7089869b9c.jpg

Additionally, when a track is loaded onto a turntable, it’s key can also be displayed on the turntable’s pitch slider (pictured above), making it easier to mix harmonically.
Because a change in pitch also changes the key of the track, the key’s value will change color to indicate that the key has changed if the pitch is adjusted by more than 3 percent.

Full Release Notes
I’ve also added a number of other changes and improvements, so be sure to read through the full release notes below.

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.1 – Turntable customization and improvements
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/d3f7b6f8d238625b171c16bb3bf86ad0e9d58297.jpg

Version 1.2.1 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds a ton of settings which allows user to customize both the appearance and handling of the turntables.

Customizing the turntable’s appearance

The appearance of the turntables can now be customized in a number of ways. 
First of all, there a re now two turntable color schemes to chose from, the classic dark (SL-1210) scheme and the new light (SL-1200) scheme also found in earlier version of Vinyl Reality.

Users can now also easily design and load their own slipmat designs by following this handy guide available on the  online documentation website.

Turntable handling settings

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/ea32c53cd6be5ba1b3b47eb109b512947e6f5a34.jpg

The user settings menu now has a separate turntable panel, which allows users to configure how the turntables handle. 
For example, setting the Slipmat Friction to high and the Motor Start / Stop Speed to instant, will make the turntables handle a lot more like a CDJ (in vinyl mode) than a regular turntable. 

Turntable spindle input

The turntable’s spindle can now also be used to make precise pitch bend corrections. 
To increase or decrease the playback speed using the spindle, first grab the spindle with the trigger (index finger) and then while grabbing slide the thumb up or down the controller’s trackpad, or move the controller’s joystick up or down. 

Full Release Notes

I’ve also added a number of other changes and small improvements, so be sure to read through the full release notes below. For more in-depth information about all of these features, you can check out the online documentation: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.0 – Valve Index and Oculus Rift S controller support
notes.content:
Version 1.2.0 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds support for several new controller types, including Valve’s Index controllers and the Oculus Rift S.

Index Controller Support

I have not yet finished the skeletal input system, which would use finger tracking and touch to interact with objects, so for now the Index controllers still use the same input input system as other controllers.
The control scheme for the Index controllers has been designed to be as intuitive and reliable as possible, but you can always modify it to your personal preferences using the SteamVR controller bindings settings.

I’ve made the “experimental” (and outdated) branch of the application, which contains an unfinished implementation of the skeletal input system, public for every one who already owns a pair of index controllers to try out. If there is enough interest, I might continue working on the skeletal input version of the application at a later date, so be sure to let me know in the comments below!

Trackpad input tweaks for mixer knobs

I’ve also changed the way rotary knobs on the mixer (ex: EQ knobs) react to trackpad input. To rotate a knob with the trackpad, you now first need to grab the knob and then slide your thumb up or down the trackpad. This action mimics rotating the knob between your thumb and index finger and should feel more natural.

I’ve also added two new trackpad related settings to the mixer’s user settings panel: 

 Invert Left Trackpad Input:
Inverts the direction the knob rotates for the left controller’s trackpad
 Trackpad Scroll Range: 
Controls how many degrees the knob rotates based on the trackpad input


Full Release notes:

 SteamVR version: Added support for Valve’s Index controllers
 Oculus version: Updated plug-ins to display correct controller models for Rift S
 Oculus version: Fixed haptic feedback (again)
 Mixer: Updated trackpad input for rotary knobs
 Mixer: Added user settings for rotary knob trackpad input
 Tutorial: Added input action hints to controllers

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.9 – Mixer Fader improvements
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/24123d0a600d3e37c21b1333b0eed476ea571143.jpg

Version 1.1.9 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update focuses on improving the functionality of the mixer’s crossfader and channel faders by making them more configurable.

Mixer Fader Settings

A new Mixer Fader Settings panel has been added to the user settings interface. Using this panel, the curves of both the crossfader and channel faders can be adjusted to adapt to different play styles or situations. 

For example, scratch DJs often prefer a crossfader with a very sharp curve for performing fast cuts, while radio DJs might prefer a smooth crossfader curve which maintains a constant output volume while fading between two tracks.

Both fader curves are displayed and updated in real-time to visualize the current settings. The curve describes the volume (y-axis) in relation to the fader’s position (x-axis).

Each of the mixer’s channels can now also be assigned to either the left or right side of the crossfader, or set to ignore the crossfader’s position completely.

Audio Settings

I’ve also slightly redesigned the Audio Settings panel and replaced the Advanced settings with an Audio Buffer Size setting, which offers users more granular control than previously. This can be useful if the recommended settings still causes a delay between the default and master audio outputs.

For more more in-depth information about these features, be sure to check out the relevant online documentation: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=user_settings

Full Release notes

 Mixer: Added fader and crossfader curve settings
 Mixer: Added crossfader assign settings
 User Settings: Redesigned audio buffer settings to give users more granular control
 User Set- tings: Improved UI lay-out and responsiveness
 SDK: Fixed issue with terrain shaders not being loaded for custom environments
 Bug Fixes: Several minor bug fixes and improvements

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.8 – Mixer Equalizer improvements
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/097d42d4651c80a6ff3beac0bcb91df9eb501f7e.jpg

Version 1.1.8 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update focuses on improving the functionality of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer as well as fixing some major bugs in the main menu.

Equalizer kill switches
Each of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer knobs now has a kill switch function which when activated cuts all the frequencies for the corresponding range (High, Mid or Low) from the audio signal playing through the channel. This effect can also be achieved by turning an equalizer knob all the way counter-clockwise, but the kill switch function allows for fast and easy toggling.

While the kill switch is active, a LED ring on the bottom of the equalizer knob will illuminate. If the knob is turned while the kill switch is active, the LED ring will flash to indicate that the adjustment has no effect.

Equalizer settings
The frequency crossover points (Low to Mid and Mid to High) and crossover slope of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer can now be configured using the new mixer settings panel inside the user settings UI. Tweaking these values can be useful to adapt the equalizer to different musical genres.

For more information about how to use the new kill switch function and equalizer settings, be sure to check out the wiki page on the topic: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=mixer

Full Release notes

 Mixer: Added kill switch function to 3 band equalizer
 Mixer: Added mixer settings panel to configure 3 band equalizer
 Bug Fix: Fixed crash in main menu affecting some users
 Bug Fix: Fixed main menu sometimes becoming unresponsive

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.7 – Further record case improvements
notes.content:
Version 1.1.7 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds a bunch of improvements and new functionality to the record case. 

The record case now automatically keeps tracks of which records have already been played and will mark them accordingly. When a track is played on one of the turntables and the output volume of the corresponding mixer channel is above a certain threshold (0.1), it will be marked in yellow in the record case’s UI.

Upon ending a session and exiting the environment (or closing the application), the history of all the tracks played will automatically be exported as a M3U8 playlist and saved in the “Vinyl Reality/History” subfolder in the user’s default music folder (ex: …/Users/username/My Music/Vinyl Reality/History).

These playlist can then be loaded into Vinyl Reality afterwards like any other playlist. The order of the tracks in the playlist matches the order in which they were originally played.

Be sure to check out the full release notes below to see what other new features have been added!

Upcoming features poll

To help me decide which features of the application to focus on in the upcoming updates, I’ve organized a small poll in the Vinyl Reality discord server. 
If you want your voice to be heard, be sure to join the Discord server and cast your vote by the beginning of next week!


Full Release notes

 Record Case: Track history is exported to a M3U8 playlist upon exiting environment

Version 1.1.6 of Vinyl Reality is now available. 

The biggest feature added in this update is the ability to load Rekordbox collections into Vinyl Reality. For those who aren’t familiar with the software, Rekordbox is a free music management and DJ app from Pioneer DJ.

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.3 – Record case playlists and improvements
notes.content:
Version 1.1.3 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This first update of the new year adds several improvements to the record case.

Playlists

The biggest new feature is the ability to load m3u and m3u8 playlists in the record case, which makes loading your track collection inside Vinyl Reality a lot easier. This format of playlists can be created in, and exported from, most DJ, media player and music management applications.

Here are a couple of possible use cases for playlists in Vinyl Reality:

 Creating playlists with tracks sorted by BPM, Artist, etc..
 Breaking up a large music collection into manageable chunks, without having to move files
 Transferring playlists between different apps


If playlists files are found in the current directory, they will be displayed in the record case list beneath the directories. To load a playlist, simply select it and use the enter action to open it. If an audio file included in a playlist is missing, it will be marked red in the record case list.

Performance

I’ve also spent a lot of time improving the performance of the record case. In previous versions, loading folders or playlists which contain a large amount of tracks could take a long time, but with this update it should be almost instantaneous.

Full release notes:

 Record Case: Added support for loading m3u and m3u8 playlists
 Record Case: Improved performance when loading a large amount of tracks
 Record Case: Fixed some tags not being parsed correctly
 Tech: Updated 3rd party libraries
 Bug Fix: Fixed record sometimes not appearing from sleeve when scrolling through records

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.2 – SteamVR Input
notes.content:
Update 1.1.2 of Vinyl Reality has left the beta phase and is now available on the main branch.

Here’s an overview of all the input actions that can be configured:


Grab Pinch: Grab objects or input controls using the index finger (ex: sliders, knobs, etc..)
Grap Grip: Grab objects or input controls using the entire hand (ex: vinyl records, etc…)
Button Press: Press buttons (ex: start button, cue button, streaming console pads, etc…)
Toggle Virtual Headphones: Toggle virtual headphones channel
Joystick Position: Scroll through the record case list or make precise input control adjustments by moving the controller’s joystick
Trackpad Slide: Scroll through the record case list or make precise input control adjustments by sliding the thumb over the controller’s trackpad (Requires Trackpad Position to be assigned)
Trackpad Positon: Position of the thumb on the controller’s trackpad
Record Case Open Menu: Open radial navigation menu in record case (Requires Trackpad Position to be assigned)
Record Case Enter: Enter selected folder in record case
Record Case Return: Return to previous folder in record case
Toggle User Settings: Toggle user settings panel
UI Click: Interact with UI elements in the main menu and user settings panels

Feature: Added support for SteamVR input system
Turntable: Fixed strobe dot speed on turntable platter

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.6 – Polish and Performance
notes.content:
Version 1.0.6 of Vinyl Reality has been released just in time for the weekend.

This update focuses on polishing existing features, and improving the overall performance of the application.

One of the biggest improvement is the addition of the “Minimize Master Output Delay” option in the advanced audio settings panel. Enabling this option should reduce the delay between the default and master audio outputs to a minimum, making it possible to mix using the speakers as a reference.

The turntable code has been completely rewritten to make it more robust, and to fix the issue where the playback position of records would drift. A small arrow has been added to the record label, which points to the turntable’s needle, when at the start of a track.

A lot of other code has also been rewritten, to make it easier to add new upcoming features. If I have done my job well, none of these code changes should not be noticeable, but in case you should encounter a new bug, be sure to report it.

Full Release Notes:

Audio Settings: Redesigned UI panel to be more clear 
Audio Settings: Added experimental “Minimize Master Output Delay” option
Audio Settings: Disabled master output by default
Turntable: Fixed playback position drifting issue
Vinyl Record: Fixed waveform not loading in certain edge cases


Thanks to all beta testers who helped test this new version ;)

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.5 – Streaming Console
notes.content:
Version 1.0.5 of Vinyl Reality is now available.

The goal of this update was to make footage recorded with Vinyl Reality more interesting and engaging for your audience to watch, by enabling you to select different camera perspectives to display on the desktop mirror, while recording or streaming your set.

You can switch between the different cameras by selecting the corresponding pad on the bottom row of the new streaming console. The leftmost pad, conveniently labeled HMD,  will display the feed from your headset.

To see what’s possible, be sure to check out this video that was recorded live using the features of the streaming console:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTJo09_I7Dw

The streaming console also replaces the old audio recorder and adds some extra functionality, including a display which shows the duration and filename of the current recording. 

Please note that the record button on the streaming console only records audio and NOT video. To record or stream video footage, it’s recommend to use an external tool like OBS Studio, which is free and easy to setup.

The streaming console is currently only available in the brand new Recording Studio environment, which was designed to be as optimized as possible and should allow you to record your sessions without any performance issues. This environment also includes a screen which displays the feed from the external cameras when they’re activated.

For the next update (1.0.6) I don’t plan to add any new features, but instead I’ll be focusing on improving performance and polishing the content that is already there. This should give me a good foundation to start work on the next major update (1.1.0), which will add a new club environment with interactive light shows and special effects.

Full Release Notes:

Added streaming console
Added Recording Studio environment
 Removed old audio recorder
Optimized rendering performance


If you record your set using the new features added in this update, be sure to share them in the Community Hub!

I would like to encourage anyone who encounters an issue while using Vinyl Reality to report it, either by starting a discussion in the community hub or by sending a mail to support (at) entropi-games (dot) com.

Full release notes:

BUG Fix: Failed to read BPM meta data when Windows decimal symbol was set to comma
BUG Fix: Failed to load directory content in record case when user had no access permission

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.4 – Record Case improvements
notes.content:
It took a bit longer than usual, but version 1.0.4 of Vinyl Reality is now available! 

This update focuses on improving the record case's functionality. New features include support for loading several new file formats and displaying track meta data, including BPM.

If a file contains meta data about the track's BPM (Beats Per Minute), this value can now be shown on the turntable's pitch slider. This can be a useful feature for beginners who want to for example practice their beatmatching techniques. This option can easily be disabled using the settings panel on the application's display mirror.

If a track does not yet contain BPM meta data, it can be added by analyzing it in an external application such as Traktor or MixMeister.

Due to the reading of meta data, opening folders which contain a lot of tracks will now take significantly longer than before, but this will be optimized in the next update. The next update will also add several tools to make streaming your Vinyl Reality sessions more interesting and entertaining. 

Full release notes:

Added support for loading FLAC, OGG, WAV, WMA and AIF file formats
Record case UI now displays Artist, Title and BPM meta data instead of file name
Added column to record case UI to display directory file count or track BPM value
Added BPM to pitch slider UI
Added BPM to record label
Added BPM user settings panel to display mirror
Added trackpad / thumbstick input for crossfader
Improved readability of record case UI
Improved readability of vinyl record grooves

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.3 – Vinyl record grooves
notes.content:
In previous versions of Vinyl Reality, the grooves displayed on the vinyl records were static and identical for each track. With this update, each track you play is analyzed, and the grooves of the record will accurately match the corresponding track's structure.

This makes it a lot easier to anticipate changes in the music, as you can easily spot breakdowns, drops and other elements by simply looking at the record. I believe that with the addition of these latest features, Vinyl Reality now offers a very solid and usable DJing experience in VR. 

The next update, which is scheduled to be released after the holidays, will focus on improving the record case's functionality and adding a BPM (Beats Per Minute) display. For more details, be sure to check out the Early Access roadmap

Full release notes:

Visualized track structure on vinyl records
Lowered minimum height of DJ workstation
Increased amount of records to be stored in memory simultaneously
Added tips to loading screen
Minor bug fixes

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.2 – DJ Workstation
notes.content:
Version 1.0.2 of Vinyl Reality is now available. 

The main feature added in this update is the new DJ workstation, which allows users to adjust the height and angle of their DJ equipment. This should reduce neck strain caused by the weight of the VR headset after looking down at the DJ equipment for an extended period of time.

The DJ workstation is available in the Attic scene and can be controlled using the two handles in the center of the workstation’s top. The left handle controls the angle, and the handle on the right controls the height.

Some other small improvements have also been added:

Replaced textures of turntable with a darker version, to reduce glare and eye strain
Increased size of vinyl record trigger so they can picked up from the floor when dropped
Exit sign now lights up when selected
Improved audio signal flow

notes.title: Added support for Oculus Rift and Touch controllers – Update EA v1.0.1
notes.content:
I've just released version 1.0.1 of the application, which adds support for the Oculus Rift and Touch controllers.

All of the input that used the Vive trackpad has been rewritten to work with the Oculus Touch controller's thumbstick or buttons. I've also added separate tutorial instructions for Oculus users, so be sure to go through it again if you've already completed it.

This new version also includes some small tweaks and fixes which affect none Oculus users as well.

Full release notes:

Added support for Oculus Rift and Touch controllers
Added separate tutorial instructions for Oculus users
Improved audio resampling quality
Slightly reduced Vive trackpad sensitivity for turntable pitch slider
